elements.evidence: Rendered Section 12.4 now reads "Customer may solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee." The prohibitory operator ("shall not solicit, hire, or employ"), the 24-month tail and the "regardless of how the employee applies" language are gone, so no non-solicitation or no-hire obligation binds Customer anywhere in the rendered text; Section 12.3 independently confirms "Customer has made no ... no-hire commitment."

No non-solicitation covenant survives in the rendered language, so there is no mutual covenant binding Vendor either; 12.4 is now a one-way permission for Customer. This level is simply not the level pursued \u2014 the preferred (no restriction at all) is stronger for Customer.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction exists after the edit, so nothing extends beyond Services-involved personnel.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the 24-month tail was deleted and no durational covenant remains to measure.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no restriction remaining, general advertisements are unrestricted; Section 12.3 also preserves hiring of "any person who responds to general recruitment."

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the "regardless of how the employee applies" language that captured unsolicited approaches is deleted and no covenant remains.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The words "hire, or employ" now appear in a permissive sentence ("Customer may solicit, hire, or employ"), so no no-hire prohibition survives.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the sole element ("Customer has no non-solicitation restriction.") is met in operative language, not merely promised in the margin comment.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only Section 12.4 \u2014 flipping the prohibitory operator and striking the 24-month duration and the anti-carve-out phrase, each of which is the target restriction itself. Section 12.3 and all other favourable language are retained verbatim; no survival tails, procedures or extra obligations were added.

The retained permissive sentence overlaps only loosely with Section 12.3 (which addresses general-recruitment responders and the absence of a no-hire commitment) and does not duplicate an operative obligation or contradict it, so the overlap does not defeat minimality.

Preserves intent: no other paragraph cross-references Section 12.4, the numbering is unchanged, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling; the previous internal conflict between 12.3 and 12.4 is resolved rather than created.

Fallback is not satisfied (no mutual covenant exists), but that is immaterial \u2014 the checklist is complete at the preferred level, which is more favourable to Customer, and the comment properly offers the compliant fallback construct if Vendor requires a covenant.
Severity uplift is warranted on the original clause: it was walk-away territory (express no-hire covering all Vendor employees for 24 months with no carve-outs), not merely a fallback miss.
